fossil
The papersThe code

Missing covariates in Cox models, dug back up.

29 results: 4 exact, 7 agree, 15 partly agree, 1 differ, 2 not attempted. The lost simulation was rebuilt from the paper as an R package and run again, and every plotted point was read back out of the paper's own figures.

See every result
Marshall et al. 2010BMC Med Res Methodol 10:7 Missing covariate data in prognostic models Fig. 1AgreesFig. 2Partly agreesFig. 3Partly agreesFig. 4Partly agreesFig. 5Partly agreesFig. 6Partly agreesFig. 7Partly agreesFig. 8Partly agreesTables 1 and 3AgreesMain claimExact In the overlay, ink is theirs and green is ours

Fig. 1

Fig. 1. Histograms of the covariates of the breast cancer data (a) and of the transformed continuous covariates (b). Ours from TH.data::GBSG2 with R's default breaks.

Agrees
Fig. 1, histograms of the covariates (a) and the transformed covariates (b)
82 of 82 values, Agrees

Fig. 2

Fig. 2. Average coefficient estimates by method and amount of MAR missingness; dashed lines: true value and 0.5 SE either side.

Partly agrees
Fig. 2, coefficient estimates under MAR
301 of 333 values, Partly agrees

Most points fall within Monte Carlo error. Most of the 32 misses are estimates of X2, X3, X4 and X5 at 50 and 75% (five at 25%), mostly MI and SI, where our MIX without truncating, MICE-PMM and SI are further from or nearer the truth than the paper's. The offset of the true values does not explain them; the 2004 to 2005 package versions could not be tested.

Fig. 3

Fig. 3. Average SE by method and amount of MAR missingness; dashed line: empirical SE with no missing data.

Partly agrees
Fig. 3, average SEs under MAR
164 of 333 values, Partly agrees

Every point of X1, X4 and X6 misses by a near-constant factor across methods and levels (ours 0.83 to 0.91, 1.12 to 1.29 and 0.83 to 0.87 times the paper's, medians 0.86, 1.14 and 0.86), close to the ratio of their empirical SEs with no missing data (0.86, 1.14, 0.87): the generated covariates differ (see the reference lines). Keeping the binaries' correlations moves the X1 and X6 SEs past the paper's. The other misses (X2, X5) are MI SEs at 50 and 75%.

Fig. 4

Fig. 4. Coverage of the true value by the 95% interval under MAR; dashed lines: 80, 90 and 95%.

Partly agrees
Fig. 4, coverage under MAR
322 of 333 values, Partly agrees

Nearly all points fall within binomial error; the misses are X3 coverage of the MI methods at 50 and 75%, where our MICE-PMM and MIX without truncating cover the true value more often than the paper's, as their X3 estimates in Fig. 2 are less biased.

Fig. 5

Fig. 5. Mean Wald p-value of each covariate under MAR; dashed line: 0.05.

Partly agrees
Fig. 5, mean p-values under MAR
295 of 333 values, Partly agrees

Most misses are X6, whose mean p-value is lower in our run at every level and method, as its SE is about 14% smaller (Fig. 3); the rest are scattered MI points for X2 to X5.

Fig. 6

Fig. 6. Model performance under MAR: (a) mean p-value of the likelihood ratio test, (b) Nagelkerke R2, (c) D statistic, (d) predicted 2-year survival.

Partly agrees
Fig. 6, model performance under MAR (LR p, R2, D, 2-year survival)
125 of 148 values, Partly agrees

Two gaps. The pooled likelihood ratio p-values after MI are below 3 x 10^-6 in our run against up to 0.0046 in the paper; no pooling rule we tried gives the paper's values. Complete-case R2, D and 2-year survival rise with missingness in our run (2-year survival 0.805 at 75% against 0.760): reversing X5's time term brings survival to 0.771 but leaves R2 and D high.

Fig. 7

Fig. 7. Coefficient estimates of X2 to X5 for four MI methods under MAR and MNAR.

Partly agrees
Fig. 7, coefficients of X2 to X5 under MAR and MNAR
119 of 140 values, Partly agrees

The MAR series match as in Fig. 2. Under MNAR our X4 estimates (every MI method shown) and X3 with MICE are further from the truth than the paper's at 50 and 75% (X4 with MICE-PMM at 75%: -0.00049 against -0.00036); X3 with MICE-PMM is nearer. The scale of X3's own term does not explain it.

Fig. 8

Fig. 8. Coverage of X2 to X4 for four MI methods under MAR and MNAR.

Partly agrees
Fig. 8, coverage of X2 to X4 under MAR and MNAR
94 of 105 values, Partly agrees

The misses are X3 coverage at 50 and 75%, following the X3 estimates of Fig. 7: under MNAR our MICE covers the true value in 12% of replicates at 75% against the paper's 33%; under MAR our MICE-PMM covers it more often (64% against 49%).

The text's 'approximately 35%' is a rounded figure: the stated hazards (0.0002 for censoring against 0.00027 exp(LP) for events) give 36.4% censored in our run and 36.6% with every variant of our generator.
Missingness design: incomplete cases, shares and overlaps (Methods text)Partly agrees22 of 40 values
  • 18 of 40 points outside their Monte Carlo tolerance:
  • incomplete cases at 5% (MCAR): paper 5, ours 5.278
  • incomplete cases at 10% (MCAR): paper 10, ours 10.49
  • X3 share of incomplete at 10% (MCAR): paper 70, ours 66.43
  • X2 share of incomplete at 10% (MCAR): paper 55, ours 52.26
  • both X2X3 share of incomplete at 10% (MCAR): paper 35, ours 32.85
  • both X8X3 share of incomplete at 10% (MCAR): paper 5, ours 4.222
  • incomplete cases at 25% (MCAR): paper 25, ours 25.75
  • X3 share of incomplete at 25% (MCAR): paper 70, ours 67.98
  • X2 share of incomplete at 25% (MCAR): paper 55, ours 53.08
  • both X2X3 share of incomplete at 25% (MCAR): paper 35, ours 33.98
  • incomplete cases at 50% (MCAR): paper 50, ours 50.76
  • X3 share of incomplete at 50% (MCAR): paper 70, ours 68.96
  • X2 share of incomplete at 50% (MCAR): paper 55, ours 54.12
  • both X2X3 share of incomplete at 50% (MCAR): paper 35, ours 34.34
  • incomplete cases at 75% (MCAR): paper 75, ours 73.93
  • X3 share of incomplete at 75% (MCAR): paper 70, ours 70.91
  • X2 share of incomplete at 75% (MCAR): paper 55, ours 56.11
  • both X2X3 share of incomplete at 75% (MCAR): paper 35, ours 35.64
Each covariate is missing in exactly its share of all cases (X3 at 25%: 67.98% of 25.75% incomplete cases is 17.50% of all cases, the design's 0.70 x 25%), but the overall share of incomplete cases runs 0.3 to 0.8 points above the target because only three pairs of indicators are tied (X5 and X3 or X8 and X2 can be missing together by chance). The shares of incomplete cases then fall slightly below the stated ones. The paper's numbers are design targets ('approximately'), and how it tied the other pairs is not stated.

Keeping the binaries' observed correlations takes the X1 and X6 SEs past the paper's (0.0064 and 0.132 against 0.0060 and 0.119, ours 0.0051 and 0.104); the unrounded coefficients move X2's true value from 0.0517 to 0.0513 (paper 0.0507); the X4 SE and the larger magnitudes stay open.

R package misscox and its tutorialAgrees

The main claim holds: MICE-PMM without transformation is the least biased MI method for the skewed covariates, stays within 10% bias at 25% (MAR), and is more than 0.5 SE from the truth at 50% under MAR, MCAR and the combined mechanism, and every MI method is more than 0.5 SE off for X3 under MNAR from 25%. The text contradicts its own figures in 18 claim fields; the 12 where our run agrees with the figures are counted as paper errors. The claims that differ follow the generated covariates and the newer imputation packages (open).

What stayed buried

  • The simulation code, its seeds and its 1000 data sets were never released.
  • How the paper's binary covariates kept their correlations: ours lose some, and the SEs of age and menopausal status come out about 14% smaller.
  • How the paper pooled the likelihood ratio test after imputation: no rule we tried gives its p-values.
  • The 2004 to 2005 imputation packages: mice 1.13.1 is gone, the others do not build on today's R.

The main claim holds: MICE-PMM without transformation is the least biased MI method for the skewed covariates, stays within 10% bias at 25% (MAR), and is more than 0.5 SE from the truth at 50% under MAR, MCAR and the combined mechanism, and every MI method is more than 0.5 SE off for X3 under MNAR from 25%. The text contradicts its own figures in 18 claim fields; the 12 where our run agrees with the figures are counted as paper errors. The claims that differ follow the generated covariates and the newer imputation packages (open).

What we matched

How each part of the paper's method was rebuilt.

Data
GBSG2 from the CRAN package TH.data: 686 patients, the eight covariates of Table 1.
Cohorts
Multivariate normal on the transformed scale, back-transformed, cut and truncated; exponential event and censoring times.
Missingness
Logistic models per covariate with Table 3's odds ratios, four mechanisms, five levels.
Methods
CC, SI and seven MI methods with norm, mix, mice and Hmisc, 20 imputations.
Analysis
The full Cox model, Rubin's rules, Li's pooled test, R2, D and 2-year survival.

Missing covariates in Cox models came back from the paper's text, its data and its own vector figures.
